--- title: "[Graph.get_node_df()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get nodes as a Polars DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7694-L7798){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Exports all nodes and their attributes to a Polars DataFrame for tabular analysis. Each row represents a node, with columns for the node ID and any attributes set on nodes. The DataFrame always includes 'id', 'label', and 'type' as the first three columns, sorted by `id` in ascending order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A Polars DataFrame with mandatory columns 'id', 'label', 'type' (first three), followed by other attributes and 'degree'. Empty DataFrame if graph has no nodes. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - the 'id', 'label', and 'type' columns are always present (first three columns) - if a node has no label, the label column will contain `None` - if a node has no type attribute, the type column will contain `None` - rows are sorted by id in ascending order - other attributes not present on a node will have `None` values - the 'degree' column is always last ## Examples {.doc-examples} Export nodes to DataFrame: ::: {#3eb87e4c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", type="user", score=95) .add_node(label="B", type="admin", score=88) .add_node(label="C", type="user", score=92) ) df = graph.get_node_df() # Returns ['id', 'label', 'type', 'score', 'degree'] df.columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['id', 'label', 'type', 'score', 'degree'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cd455af7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns (3, 5) df.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 5) ``` ::: ::: We could calculate statistics on node attributes. Let's compute the average score and count of users: ::: {#74183414 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl df["score"].mean() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 91.66666666666667 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#05f5960e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} user_count = df.filter(pl.col("type") == "user").height ``` ::: Let's now filter the table down to the higher-degree nodes. ::: {#8d68ee14 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.filter(pl.col("degree") > 5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
